messages.content: 你能給我盧浮宮博物館未來3個月的展覽資訊嗎？然後告訴我巴黎地區最好的意式和中式餐廳嗎？

function.name: restaurant_info

food_type.description: Type of cuisine for which to find restaurants. Default is 'all' if not specified.

function.name: exhibition_info
function.description: Get exhibition information for a specific museum. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

month.description: Number of upcoming months for which to retrieve exhibition details. Default is 1 if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants two things:

1. Exhibition info for Louvre Museum for next 3 months. Use function exhibition_info with museum_name="Louvre Museum", month=3.

2. Restaurant info for Paris region for Italian and Chinese cuisines. The function restaurant_info can only return one type at a time? It has optional food_type param. We need best restaurants for both types. So we might call twice: once for Italian, once for Chinese. Or maybe we can combine? The function signature says food_type?: "Italian" | "Chinese" | "Mexican" | "American". So we can specify either. But we want best restaurants for both. We could call twice or ask for all? The default is 'all', but we want specifically Italian and Chinese. So we should call twice.

We need to output the results after calling functions. According to instruction, we should not provide explanation, just the function calls. Then after receiving responses, we will format them nicely.

Thus we first call exhibition_info. Then call restaurant_info twice. We'll do separate calls.
